name: MS-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Trent Kelly running with large cash advantage
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Kelly at 96%
model.rationale: Kelly is a well-funded incumbent in an R+18 district, and prediction markets give him about a 96% chance with no contrary polling evidence. The fundamentals-based margin of roughly -12 to -17 points leaves Johnson only a remote path.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Johnson within single digits, or a major scandal involving Kelly, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Mississippi's first district is deeply Republican, with a partisan lean of about eighteen points toward the GOP. Trent Kelly, the incumbent since 2015, is running for another term after clearing his primary, and he holds a clear financial edge: roughly $864,000 on hand to challenger Cliff Johnson's $150,000. Johnson, a Democrat, has raised a modest sum with no reported outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets price Kelly near 96%, consistent with a comfortable incumbent win in a seat this red. A Libertarian candidate also appears on the ballot but is not a factor.
